AGZ learns to play Go by using supervised learning with a loss that is based on a Monte-Carlo Tree search (MCTS), where the MCTS is used to generate the training data and the loss function is based on MCTS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a formal understanding of the two innovations of AGZ.

(1) we show that the policy learning step in AGZ is equivalent to minimizing the cross-entropy between the MCTS policy and the target policy; (2) we show that self-play in AGZ is a special case of {\em policy gradient} with an {\em implicit} policy gradient estimator; (3) we show that AGZ's policy gradient estimator is {\em biased} and propose a {\em biased} variance reduction technique for policy gradient algorithms.
